name: Backdigital Job Board for Onapply
author: backdigital

sections.description:
Backdigital Job Board for Onapply connects a public Onapply JSON feed to WordPress and displays the available jobs as a customizable job board. A public Onapply career feed URL is required. This plugin is an independent product by Backdigital and is not an official Onapply plugin.

The free version includes:

  • Job listings from a public Onapply JSON feed
  • Filters for location, department, and employment type
  • Pagination and listing limits
  • Shortcode [backjobo_jobs]
  • Basic color, text, and button settings
  • Links to the public Onapply job detail page
  • Transient cache management

[//]: # fs_premium_only_begin
Pro adds:

  • Onapply API integration with a safe public-feed cross-check
  • Internal job detail pages and readable URLs
  • Extended design controls
  • SEO titles, meta descriptions, and canonical URLs
  • JobPosting JSON-LD and Google Jobs preparation
  • System checks, debugging, and extended cache tools
    [//]: # fs_premium_only_end

External services

This plugin connects to the following external services:

  • Onapply: The configured JSON feed URL is requested from the website server when job listings are displayed or the cache is refreshed. The Onapply endpoint may receive technical connection data such as the website server IP address and HTTP headers.
  • Freemius: Freemius provides optional licensing, upgrades, updates, account functions, and checkout. Data is transferred after consent during Freemius onboarding or when licensing, account, support, or purchase functions are used. Privacy information: https://freemius.com/privacy/

Privacy

The plugin stores the configured feed URL and display settings in the WordPress database. Job data is stored temporarily in the WordPress transient cache. The plugin does not create applicant profiles and does not process applications. Applications are handled by Onapply.
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate the plugin.
  2. Open “Backdigital Job Board for Onapply” in the WordPress admin area.
  3. Enter the public Onapply JSON feed URL.
  4. Add the shortcode [backjobo_jobs] to a page.
  5. Optionally configure filters, colors, text, limits, and pagination.
sections.faq:
Where can I find the Onapply feed URL?

In Onapply, open Settings > Career Page > Feed and select the JSON feed URL.

Does “Learn more” open the job description?

Yes. The free version links to the public Onapply job detail page instead of directly opening the application form whenever the feed provides enough information.

Are my settings retained when I upgrade to Pro?

Yes. Free and Pro use the same WordPress option key.

Does Pro guarantee visibility in Google Jobs?

No. Pro prepares the technical structure and JobPosting data. Google decides whether a job is displayed.

  • Pro: Internal detail links now jump directly to the rendered job detail area.
  • Replaced folder-name based Free/Pro build detection with premium-file detection.

1.4.1

  • Standardized all plugin-owned functions, classes, constants, options, transients, actions, query variables, menu slugs, and shortcodes with the unique backjobo prefix.
  • Replaced legacy shortcodes with [backjobo_jobs].

1.3.9

  • Renamed the plugin to “Backdigital Job Board for Onapply” to clearly indicate independent third-party integration.
  • Changed the plugin folder, main file, and text domain to backdigital-job-board-onapply.
  • Updated the WordPress.org contributor and removed an invalid external privacy URL.

1.3.7

  • Aligned the previous plugin folder, main file, and text domain during the initial WordPress.org submission.

1.3.6

  • Changed the WordPress.org readme short description and documentation to English.
  • Changed Tested up to to the required major WordPress version format.
  • Added documented PHPCS exclusions for read-only public filter parameters.
  • Expanded internal prefixes used by the Freemius bootstrap and plugin globals.

1.3.5

  • Completed the WordPress.org plugin headers.
  • Added external service and privacy documentation.
  • Switched public feed requests to wp_safe_remote_get().
  • Removed direct database access from cache clearing.

1.3.4

  • Unified Free, Pro, and core version numbers.
  • Finalized the shared Free/Pro release candidate.

1.3.3

  • Improved the Free-to-Pro activation flow.
  • Display the account link only after a Freemius account is connected.

1.3.2

  • Free: “Learn more” now reliably opens the public Onapply detail page.

1.3.1

  • Display the reset button only when a filter is active.
